title: How pliers multiply your grip
examples: Why are pliers so much stronger than fingers?
Why do pliers have long handles and short jaws?

explain.say: Pliers are two first-class levers crossed at a rivet, which is the pivot. Your hand squeezes the long handles, and the short jaws grip on the other side.
Your hand presses far from the pivot, so even a gentle squeeze makes a big turning effect.
The jaws are five times closer to the pivot than your hand, so to balance the turning effect they press with about five times the force. That grips a nut tightly or bends wire.
The trade-off is distance: your hands move a long way while the jaws close only a little. Cutting pliers put hardened edges close to the pivot for even more force.

faq.a: Pliers are two levers joined at a pivot. Squeezing the long handles makes the short jaws close with a much bigger force, because the jaws are closer to the pivot than your hand.

faq.q: Why do pliers have long handles?
faq.a: Long handles put your hand far from the pivot. The further away you push, the bigger the turning effect, so you get more grip from the same squeeze.
Short jaws keep the gripping point close to the pivot, so the force there is multiplied the most.
asks: Why do pliers have short jaws?

faq.a: Mechanical advantage is how many times a machine multiplies your force: load divided by effort. Pliers with handles five times longer than the jaws have a mechanical advantage of about 5.
asks: How much do pliers multiply force?

faq.a: No. The jaws push harder but move a much smaller distance than your hands, so the work done is the same at best.

facts: Mechanical advantage equals load divided by effort.
For a lever, the ideal mechanical advantage is the effort's distance from the pivot divided by the load's distance.

quiz.say: Pliers have handles 10 cm and jaws 2 cm from the pivot. You squeeze with 20 newtons. What is the force at the jaws?
quiz.show: Pliers have handles 10 cm and jaws 2 cm from the pivot. You squeeze with 20 newtons. What is the force at the jaws?
quiz.why: The ratio is 10 divided by 2, which is 5, and 5 times 20 is 100 newtons.

wrong.0: That doubles the force, but the ratio is 5, not 2.
wrong.2: The jaws push harder than your hand, not less.
